consensus_summary: Primary consensus across responses identifies 'life'/'the life' as eternal divine life (zoe) embodied in and given through Jesus Christ, or Christ himself as that life, anchored in Johannine texts (John 1:4; 11:25; 14:6; 17:3; 1 John 5:11-12 etc.) and related NT passages; alternatives include biological existence, present abundant/renewed life, covenant flourishing via fidelity, resurrection life, and Spirit-mediated life, but these are secondary or context-specific.
book_summary: Covenant existence — the life the law produces.
consensus_core_identification: Christ himself / eternal divine (zoe) life given in and through Christ
book_core_identification: covenant existence produced by the law
boundary_disagreement: Book reassigns the primary sense of 'the life' from the Christological/zoe referent (consensus core) to law-generated covenant existence, elevating OT obedience texts (Deut 30; Lev 18) as definitional while treating the common Christ identification as merely 'commonly taught' rather than central.
material_contradiction: Consensus core equates 'the life' with Christ/zoe (often contrasted with law in NT); book equates it with what the law produces via covenant obedience—claims that cannot both hold as the primary identification of the same term in the same theological sense.
rationale: Minimum cores are non-equivalent: consensus primary is the person/gift of Christ as divine life; book primary is the product of law-keeping. Alternatives list covenant flourishing (e.g., Deut 30), so the book is not wholly unattested, yet presenting that as the entry (while noting the Christ view as common) requires replacing rather than refining or overlapping the consensus core. Extension therefore concerns a different referent, not a subset/superset of the same cases. Citations mix OT law-life texts with Christ-as-life texts, confirming the divergence rather than resolving it.
strongest_objection: NT usage (esp. Johannine 'I am the life' and statements that life is in the Son, not the law—cf. Gal 3:21; Rom 10:5 vs. 10:6-10) makes the law-product identification incompatible with the dominant sense of 'the life'.
